simple.meaning: עֲבִי (ʻăbîy) is a Hebrew object word meaning “density , i.e. depth or width.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 7:26. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H5672. abi or obi עֲבִי noun [masculine] thickness ; — construct ׳ע מָגִנָּיו נַּבֵּי Job 15:26 the thickness (stoutness) of the bosses of his shields (in figurative); suffix עָבְיוֺ its thickness , of the molten sea 1Kin 7:26 2Chr 4:5 ; of pillar Jer 52:21 . — 2Chr 4:17 see following — Under עבה belongs perhaps also הֶעָנָן בְּעַב Exod 19:9 (read בַּעֲבִי ?) in the thickness of the clouds, compare Bu ThLz 1892 (3), 63 Kö ii 1, 86 .

occurrences.englishText: It was a hand width thick. Its brim was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.

It was a handbreadth thick; and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It received and held three thousand baths.‡ A bath is about 5.6 U. S. gallons or 21.1 liters, so 3,000 baths is about 16,800 gallons or 63.3 kiloliters.
